question: In which of the following sessions did the Indian National Congress decide to boycott the Simon Commission?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Madras session**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Indian National Congress decided to boycott the Simon Commission during the **Madras session held in 1927**.
 
• The Simon Commission, appointed in 1927 by the British government, faced opposition as it **lacked any Indian representation**.
 
• The boycott of the Simon Commission was a significant step in India's freedom movement as it demonstrated **unified resistance to colonial policies.**
 
• During the Madras session, leaders like **Motilal Nehru and Jawaharlal Nehru** played pivotal roles in advocating for the boycott.
 
• The slogan "**Simon Go Back**" became a rallying cry for Indians, showcasing widespread discontent with British rule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Simon Commission:**

 
 
• It was constituted in 1927 to review the working of the Government of India Act, 1919, and suggest constitutional reforms.
 
• The absence of Indian members in the commission led to massive protests and its rejection by Indian leaders.
 
 
 
• **Madras Session of 1927:**
 
 
• It was a landmark session of the Indian National Congress presided over by **Dr. M.A. Ansari**.
 
• The decision to boycott the Simon Commission was one of the key resolutions passed during this session.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Boycott:**
 
 
• The boycott strengthened the resolve for greater autonomy and eventually complete independence from British rule.
 
• It also led to the drafting of the **Nehru Report (1928)**, which proposed a dominion status constitution for India.
 
 
 
• **Slogan “Simon Go Back”:**
 
 
• It symbolized the unity of Indians across all regions and communities against British colonial policies.
 
• Prominent leaders like Lala Lajpat Rai opposed the commission, and his death due to police brutality during protests further intensified the resistance.
